name: exit()
description: Terminates the calling process and releases its resources. The kernel calls do_exit() to set the process state to TASK_DEAD, release the mm_struct and file descriptors, notify the parent via SIGCHLD, and transition the process to a zombie until the parent reaps it via wait4().

main_flow.title: User Space — exit(status) call
main_flow.description: The user-space program invokes exit(status) (or _exit() / _Exit()), which calls the exit_group syscall to terminate the entire thread group. The C library wrapper places the status code in the exit argument, then issues the syscall instruction to trap into the kernel.

detail_nodes.title: glibc exit() wrapper
detail_nodes.description: The glibc exit() function performs atexit-registered cleanup handlers, flushes stdio buffers, closes streams, then calls the _exit() system call (NR_exit_group = 231 on x86-64) to enter the kernel. The status argument (0-255) is passed in the %rdi register.

detail_nodes.title: SYSCALL_DEFINE1(exit_group, int, error_code)
detail_nodes.description: The exit_group syscall terminates all threads in the process group. On x86-64, the syscall number 231 is placed in %rax, and the exit status is passed in %rdi. The syscall instruction traps into the kernel entry point.

detail_nodes.title: do_group_exit() — signal all threads
detail_nodes.description: do_group_exit() sends SIGKILL to all other threads in the thread group via zap_other_threads(), then falls through to do_exit() for the current thread. This ensures the entire process group terminates together.

main_flow.title: Kernel Entry — do_exit()
main_flow.description: do_exit() is the central kernel function for process termination. It sets the process state to PF_EXITING, disables preemption, and begins releasing all process resources in a carefully ordered sequence.

detail_nodes.title: do_exit() entry
detail_nodes.description: do_exit() in kernel/exit.c is the core process termination function. It first sets PF_EXITING on the task flags to prevent signal delivery, then calls exit_mm() to release the memory descriptor, followed by exit_files() to close file descriptors, and exit_fs() to release filesystem resources.

detail_nodes.title: exit_signals() — block all signal delivery
detail_nodes.description: exit_signals() sets the task's blocked signal mask to block all signals, clears pending signals, and prevents any new signal delivery to the dying process. This ensures a clean termination without interruption.

detail_nodes.title: PF_EXITING flag
detail_nodes.description: The PF_EXITING flag in task_struct->flags marks the process as being in the process of exiting. Once set, the scheduler will not migrate this task, signal delivery is blocked, and futex operations are short-circuited.

main_flow.title: MM Release — exit_mm() → mmput() → release mm_struct
main_flow.description: exit_mm() releases the process's memory descriptor. It detaches the mm_struct from the task, decrements its reference count via mmput(), and if the count reaches zero, frees all page tables, VMAs, and the mm_struct itself.

detail_nodes.title: exit_mm() — detach mm_struct from task
detail_nodes.description: exit_mm() in kernel/exit.c sets task->mm to NULL (the task no longer has an address space), then calls mmput() to decrement the mm_struct reference count. If this was the last reference, mmput() triggers full memory teardown.

detail_nodes.title: mmput() — decrement mm reference count
detail_nodes.description: mmput() decrements the mm_struct's mm_users count. When the count reaches zero, it calls exit_mmap() to tear down all VMAs and page tables, then mmdrop() to free the mm_struct itself.

detail_nodes.title: exit_mmap() — free all VMAs and page tables
detail_nodes.description: exit_mmap() walks all vm_area_struct entries in the mm, unmaps each region (freeing page table entries and decrementing page reference counts), and frees the VMA structures. This is the bulk of memory cleanup.

main_flow.title: FD Cleanup — exit_files() → put_files_struct()
main_flow.description: exit_files() closes all open file descriptors by decrementing the reference count on the files_struct. If the count reaches zero, put_files_struct() iterates the fdtable, calling filp_close() on each open file to release inodes, dentries, and filesystem resources.

detail_nodes.title: exit_files() — release file descriptor table
detail_nodes.description: exit_files() sets task->files to NULL and decrements the files_struct reference count. If this was the last reference, it triggers the full cleanup of all open file descriptors.

detail_nodes.title: put_files_struct() — close all open fds
detail_nodes.description: put_files_struct() decrements the files_struct reference count. When it reaches zero, it iterates through the fdtable, calling filp_close() for each open file descriptor, which releases the struct file, decrements inode and dentry reference counts, and calls the filesystem's release method.

detail_nodes.title: close_files() — filp_close loop
detail_nodes.description: close_files() iterates over all file descriptors in the fdtable. For each non-NULL entry, it calls filp_close(), which invokes the file's f_op->release method, decrements f_count, and if zero, frees the struct file and its associated dentry and inode.

main_flow.title: Signal Parent — do_notify_parent() → wake_up_parent()
main_flow.description: Before becoming a zombie, the exiting process notifies its parent by sending SIGCHLD. do_notify_parent() delivers the signal, sets the child's exit code in the parent's signal info, and wakes the parent if it is waiting in wait4().

detail_nodes.title: do_notify_parent() — send SIGCHLD to parent
detail_nodes.description: do_notify_parent() sends SIGCHLD to the parent process with the child's exit status. If the parent has set SA_NOCLDSTOP or SA_NOCLDWAIT, the behavior is adjusted accordingly. The signal includes the child's PID and the exit code.

detail_nodes.title: wake_up_parent() — unblock wait4() caller
detail_nodes.description: After sending SIGCHLD, the kernel wakes the parent process if it is sleeping in a wait-family syscall (wait4, waitpid, waitid). The parent can then reap the child's exit status and free the remaining task_struct.

detail_nodes.title: struct siginfo — exit status payload
detail_nodes.description: The siginfo structure carries the child's exit information to the parent: si_pid (child PID), si_status (exit code), si_utime/si_stime (CPU times), and si_code (CLD_EXITED for normal exit, CLD_KILLED for signal termination).

main_flow.title: Zombie — release_task() → zap_pid_ns_processes()
main_flow.description: After do_exit() sets the task state to TASK_DEAD, the process becomes a zombie. It retains its task_struct and PID until the parent calls wait4(). If the parent exits first, init (PID 1) inherits the child and reaps it.

detail_nodes.title: release_task() — called from wait4() path
detail_nodes.description: release_task() is called when the parent reaps the child via wait4(). It detaches the zombie from the task list, releases the PID via free_pid(), decrements the parent's signal_struct live count, and finally frees the task_struct with free_task().

detail_nodes.title: zap_pid_ns_processes() — PID namespace cleanup
detail_nodes.description: When a PID namespace is being destroyed, zap_pid_ns_processes() iterates all remaining processes in the namespace and forces them to exit. This ensures no dangling PIDs remain when a container or namespace is torn down.

detail_nodes.title: free_pid() — return PID to the bitmap
detail_nodes.description: free_pid() returns the PID number to the pidmap bitmap so it can be reused by future processes. It also decrements the struct pid reference count and frees it when the last reference is dropped.

main_flow.title: Reaped — wait4() → release_task() → task_struct freed
main_flow.description: The parent calls wait4() (or waitpid/wait) to collect the child's exit status. The kernel finds the zombie child, copies its exit code to user space, calls release_task() to free the task_struct and PID, and returns the child's PID to the parent.

detail_nodes.title: wait4() — parent reaps child
detail_nodes.description: wait4() iterates the parent's children list looking for a zombie (EXIT_ZOMBIE) child. When found, it copies the exit status to the user-provided status pointer, records resource usage (rusage), and calls release_task() to free the child's task_struct.

detail_nodes.title: do_wait() — find and reap zombie children
detail_nodes.description: do_wait() walks the children and sibling lists under tasklist_lock, looking for a child in EXIT_ZOMBIE state. When found, it collects the exit status and calls release_task(). If no zombie is found and WNOHANG is not set, it sleeps on the wait_chldexit wait queue until a child exits.

detail_nodes.title: init (PID 1) — the ultimate reaper
detail_nodes.description: If a parent exits before its children, the children are reparented to init (PID 1). init periodically calls wait4(-1, ...) to reap any orphaned children, preventing zombie processes from accumulating on the system.
